rationale: No race telemetry exists yet (iteration 0), so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 15 mm apart across x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. A 12 mm footprint is used because it spans the 25 mm tape while still resolving the centre position. The track is 0.12 m, the wheel radius is 0.03 m, and the body is 0.12 by 0.16 m at 0.8 kg, a moderate, stable platform. Controller: antisymmetric weights [-1.0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0] give a signal scaled to about +/-1. kp = 3 turns the signal into roughly 1050 PWM counts of wheel difference at full error, which should steer without saturating. kd = 0.2 damps oscillation, and ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.8 (about 3685 PWM) targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s. line_loss = last_direction recovers toward the side the robot last saw the tape. Expected outcome: completion on the oval and s-bend, with the main risk being overshoot on the slalom at this speed. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp is too low or too high for the chosen speed; (2) kd is too small to damp the slalom; (3) base_speed trades completion time against off-track or line-loss events. Next measurements: completion, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events, and steering oscillation, which together separate speed-limited from control-limited failures.
